title: Arc Length, Sector Area and Angular Speed
short: s = rθ and A = ½r²θ when θ is in radians.
trouble: Students use degrees in s = rθ.

blocks.html: In geometry you found arc length and sector area as a fraction of the whole circle, with the angle in degrees. Radians make those formulas much shorter, because a radian is already measured in radii.
With $\theta$ in radians: $$s = r\theta \qquad A = \tfrac{1}{2}r^2\theta.$$ For turning motion, angular speed is $\omega = \frac{\theta}{t}$ and the speed of a point on the rim is $v = r\omega$.

A sector of angle $\theta$ is the fraction $\frac{\theta}{2\pi}$ of the full circle. So its arc is $\frac{\theta}{2\pi} \cdot 2\pi r = r\theta$ and its area is $\frac{\theta}{2\pi} \cdot \pi r^2 = \frac{1}{2}r^2\theta$. For speed: in time $t$ a point on the rim travels the arc $s = r\theta$, so its speed is $\frac{s}{t} = r \cdot \frac{\theta}{t} = r\omega$.

blocks.cap: Change the angle and the radius. The readout computes $s = r\theta$ and $A = \frac{1}{2}r^2\theta$.

blocks.title: Arc and area
blocks.q: A sector has radius $6$ in and angle $\frac{2\pi}{3}$. Find its arc length and area.

blocks.title: Given in degrees
blocks.q: Find the arc length cut off by a $45^\circ$ angle on a circle of radius $8$ cm.

blocks.title: A spinning wheel
blocks.q: A bike wheel of radius $30$ cm turns at $100$ revolutions per minute. How fast is the bike moving?
steps: Each revolution is $2\pi$ radians, so $\omega = 100 \cdot 2\pi = 200\pi$ radians per minute.
That is about $18{,}850$ cm, or $188.5$ m, each minute.

blocks.html: Using degrees in $s = r\theta$. With $45^\circ$ and $r = 8$ you would get $s = 360$ cm, but the whole circle is only $2\pi \cdot 8 \approx 50$ cm around. Check: an arc can't be longer than the circumference unless the angle is more than a full turn.
